stem: Capital of Kingdom of Maharaja Ranjit Singh was:
expl: Zaman Shah invaded Punjab in 1798 AD. While returning, his cannons had fallen in the Jhelum River. Ranjit Singh returned them safely to Lahore. In 1799 AD, he seized Lahore and made it capital.

stem: At which place did Raja Ranjit Singh set up the Adalat-i-Ala?
expl: Maharaja Ranjit Singh set up the Adalat-i-Ala at Lahore which heard appeals from the district and provincial courts.

stem: The Treaty of Amritsar was concluded between Maharaja Ranjit Singh and
expl: Treaty of Amritsar was signed by Mr. Charles Metcalfe on behalf of British Governor general Lord Minto I and Maharaja Ranjit Singh at Amritsar on April 25, 1809 AD. According to this treaty, Ranjit Singh was to recognize the river Sutlej as the boundary and to accept the British suzerainty over his vassals across the river, and the English were to recognize the Maharaja as the sole sovereign on his side of River Sutlej.

stem: Ranjeet Singh got famous Kohinoor diamond from-
expl: Punjab was part of Ahmad Shah Abdali’s territory, but in 1772 A.D. after his death, most of the area of his empire was occupied by Sikh misls leaving Multan, Kashmir and some other smaller regions. Ranjit Singh got the opportunity to consolidate his empire as Afghans were engaged in internal fi ghts. In 1803 AD, Shah Shuja (the grandson of Ahmad Shah Abdali) sat on the throne of Kabul but Shah Mahmud (brother of Shah Shuja) along with powerful Barekzay chieftain Fateh Khan and Dost Muhammad dethroned him and occupied Kashmir and Peshawar. On that occasion, Shah Shuja asked Ranjeet Singh for help and presented him with the Kohinoor diamond.

stem: Who among the following has said, ‘God intended me to look upon all religions with one eye, that is why he took away the light from the other’?
expl: The above statement was made by Maharaja Ranjit Singh. Ranjit Singh was born on 13 Nov. 1780 A.D. at Gujranwala. When he was only 12 years old, his father Maha Singh died. A council of regency governed administration from 1792 A.D. to 1797 A.D. which included his mother, mother-in-Law and Diwan Lakhpat Rai. He assumed the powers directly in 1797. Ranjit Singh annexed Lahore (1799 A.D.), Amritsar (1802 A.D.).

stem:
Which of the following statements is/are correct in the context of the Treaty of Lahore (1846)?
I. The Maharaja left all his territories beyond the river Satluj forever.
II. The Maharaja left his rights over all the forts between the Satluj and Beas rivers in favour of the Company.
III. The English army could no longer pass through the Sikh State.
Select the correct answer from the codes given below :
expl: The British army occupied Lahore and in March 1846, forced the Sikhs to sign the Treaty of Lahore with following terms – – The Maharaja, ceded all his territories across the Sutlej river forever. – Maharaja completely relinquished his control over all the forts situated between Sutlej & Beas Rivers in favour of company. – They promised not to interfere in the administration. – The Sikhs were required to pay one and a half crore ruppes as war indemnity etc.

options.label: b
options.text: All the territories of Maharaja Duleep SIngh became part of the Indian British Empire.

options.label: c
options.text: Duleep Singh was given an annual pension of Rs. 2,50,000.

expl: By Lord Dalhousie's proclamation of March 29, 1849 A.D., the whole of Punjab was merged into the British Empire. All the territories of Maharaja Duleep Singh became part of the Indian British Empire and he was exiled to England in 1854 for study. For his relatives and also the maintenance of states’ employees, his pension was decided not less than four lakh rupees and not more than fi ve lakh rupees (minimum £40,000 and maximum £50,000) per annum.

stem: Who emerged victorious in the fi rst Anglo-Mysore War (1767-69)?
expl: First Anglo-Mysore War (1767-69 A.D.) was fought between British and Haidar Ali. He fought bravely and captured Mangalore in 1768 and reached Madras in 1769, where English in helplessness had to sign the “Treaty of Madras’ in April 1769 on the conditions of Haidar Ali.

stem: Who among the following established a modern armoury in Dindigul Mysore in 1755?
expl: In 1742 A.D., Mysore army under Venkata Raya's leadership conquered Dindigul. There were eighteen Palayams (Pallayakkars) during his reign and all these Palayams were under Dindigul Semai with Dindiguls capitals. These Palayams wanted to be independent & refused to pay taxes to Venkata Raja. In 1755 A.D., Mysore king sent Haidar Ali to Dindigul to handle the situation. Haidar Ali controlled Dindigul and became de-facto ruler & converted this fort into sepoy post. Later on he became the ruler of Mysore. In 1777, Haidar Ali appointed Purshana Mir Saheb as governor of Dindigul.

stem: British general who defeated/beat Haidar Ali in War of Porto Novo :
expl: Before this war, Haidar Ali made a front against the British with the Marathas and Nizam. In July 1780, Haidar Ali attacked Carnatic and on 10 September 1780 Colonel Baillie was defeated by the combined forces of Haidar Ali and Tipu in the Battle of Pollilur. The British segregated Nizam and Marathas from Haidar. Haidar Ali faced this complex situation fi rmly. Haidar Ali fought with General Eyre Coote in 1781 during the second Anglo-Mysore War, and British defeated Haidar Ali in War of Porto Novo (1st July, 1781)

stem: Tipu Sultan set up his capital at –

stem: Englishmen made the Treaty of Srirangapatna with–
expl: Third Anglo-Mysore War (1790-92 A.D.) ended with the Treaty of Srirangapatna (1792 A.D.). The treaty of Seringapatam (Srirangapatna) was signed in March 1792 A.D. between Tipu Sultan of Mysore and Lord Cornwallis on behalf of British East India Company. The agreement also included representative of the Nizam of Hyderabad and Maratha Empire, requiring Tipu to Cede half of his Kingdom. According to the treaty, Half of the territories of Tipu were snatched away from him and divided among Marathas, British, and Nizam. Tipu had to pay Rs. 330 lakhs as war indemnity to British as his two sons were kept hostage. These was a terms and condition in the treaty that until Tipu wouldn’t provide 3 crore rupees, his two sons will be under British protection.

expl: Maharaja Ranjit Singh set up factory at Lahore, Amritsar to manufacture cannons. Sawai Jai Singh got translated Euclid’s elements of geometry in Sanskrit.
